section_summary: The section concludes a report on Japan’s silk industry, covering price controls, supply, exports, domestic demand, and competition from rayon and nylon. It then contains correspondence and a memorandum praising and summarizing the report, a 1942 despatch on wartime silk use, and a 1941 note on proposed fur seal hunting.

subfiles.title: The Status of Japan’s Silk Industry
subfiles.doc_type: consular report, concluding pages and sources
subfiles.from: Ivan B. White, U.S. Consulate, Yokohama
subfiles.about: The concluding sections assess Japanese raw silk controls, supply and demand, and threats from competing fibers.
subfiles.summary: Government silk purchases and sales offered limited price stabilization because stored silk deteriorated. The report reviews newer levies and distribution quotas, estimates adequate supply through May 1940, and weighs silk income and foreign exchange against food production needs. It identifies rayon and especially nylon as threats to export markets. The final pages list published sources and Yokohama silk trade informants.

subfiles.title: Departmental appraisal of White’s silk industry report
subfiles.from: Department of State, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Richard F. Boyce, American Consul, Yokohama
subfiles.about: The Department rates White’s report excellent and asks that he be informed.
subfiles.summary: Praises the report’s thoroughness, completeness, and account of silk’s place in Japan’s economy.

subfiles.title: Routing note on White’s silk report
subfiles.about: Hiss forwards a memorandum on White’s report for circulation.
subfiles.summary: Requests circulation of the accompanying memorandum.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Consul White’s report, The Status of Japan’s Silk Industry
subfiles.about: The memorandum evaluates White’s study and summarizes the economic effects of Japan’s 1939 silk price rise.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum attributes rising prices to constrained supply, stronger domestic demand, currency changes, and speculation. It reviews government controls and the effects on exports, foreign exchange, cocoon farming, and food supplies. It also notes declining foreign demand, nylon’s potential threat, and Japanese dominance of silk shipments and shipping from Yokohama.

subfiles.title: Commerce Department comments on White’s silk industry report
subfiles.to: Raymond H. Geist, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Commerce Department praises White’s report and asks that its thanks be conveyed to him.
subfiles.summary: The Textile Division commends the report’s analysis, statistics, and usefulness for future silk industry questions.

subfiles.title: 1941–42 Japanese Silk Crop and Its Utilization in War-Time Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch relays a German newspaper account of Japan’s wartime silk consumption and exports.
subfiles.summary: The article estimates increased domestic silk use and describes mixed fabrics made to stretch other textile supplies. It reports resumed silk exports to Indochina in exchange for rice and corn, under Japanese government control.

subfiles.title: Note on Japanese fur seal hunting
subfiles.about: The note summarizes Vice Consul Lamm’s report on planned Japanese fur seal hunting.
subfiles.summary: Reports plans to take about 6,000 seals annually for fur, meat, oil, and medicines.
